notes: RUBRIC PERCENTAGES MATCH 2026 EXACTLY; ONLY THE SPLIT COUNTS DIFFER - derived independently from this workbook's own header rows. THE 8+ UPSET POOL HAS EXACTLY ONE WINNER. Arkansas (a 10 seed that beat 2-seed St. John's) is the only 8+ upset in the pool, so it collects the entire 5% pool as a single $3,681.50 payment. Compare 2026 (2 splits at $3,462.25) and 2024 (3 splits at $756.25). This is the sharpest rubric-behaviour difference across the three pools and is a good stress case for a split_pool engine: denominator 1.

THE 2025 BRACKET TAB WAS NEVER FILLED IN. Its cells carry only the auction assignments (winning bidder / value paid per region-seed slot); no game results, no advancing teams, and the 'Champion' cell is an empty label. All results therefore come from the payout tab's per-round columns and its '# Upsets' counts, which are the only record. I cross-checked them against the actual 2025 tournament and every event reconciles (Florida champion; Houston runner-up; Auburn and Duke in the Final Four; Arkansas 10 over Kansas 7 = 3+ and 10 over St. John's 2 = 3+ and 8+; Drake 11 over Missouri 6; Colorado State 12 over Memphis 5; McNeese 12 over Clemson 5; New Mexico 10 over Marquette 7; BYU 6 over Wisconsin 3; Ole Miss 6 over Iowa State 3). Totals 8 and 1 match the '# of splits' row.

CROSS-BOOK TRADE: secondary trade 1 is 'Sam / Zach 0.5x Lion King XBook' / 'Zach / Sam 0.5x Lion King XBook' - a 0.5x exchange involving an outside book called 'Lion King', the same counterparty structure as Calcutta IX's trade 1 (which is 0.25x). The contract's model cannot express it beyond scope='synthetic_book': no entry_label, no identifiable underlying lot, and the legs' 'Value of Traded Asset' figures (-$2,581.15625 for Sam, +$497.85 for Zach) do not correspond to anything computable from this workbook. Only the Net Trade Value (-$3,079.00625 Sam / +$3,079.00625 Zach) is reconcilable. Direction is recorded as Zach -> Sam, which is a guess: the workbook does not say who is long which side.

NO SHORT SALE in this pool - all 10 trades are long transfers of a percentage of a lot the seller actually held (except trade 1, the cross-book swap). Contrast Calcutta IX (Sam short sells Troy) and Calcutta IV (Craig shorts 20% of UConn).
